title: Band 9 Samples: How much reading do you do for your work/studies? [Why/Why not?]
passage_html:
This post contains ideas and band-9 sample answers (audio included) for the Cambridge IELTS 17 Academic Speaking Part 1 Question 2 Test 2 question:

“How much reading do you do for your work/studies? [Why/Why not?]”

Sample 1: Regularly

I engage in extensive reading for my studies, as it is imperative to stay well-informed in my field. This diligent approach not only enhances my comprehension of the subject matter but also cultivates critical thinking skills and fosters intellectual growth.

Sample 2: Regularly

Reading constitutes a significant portion of my academic endeavors. I frequently immerse myself in academic journals, textbooks, and online resources, as it is crucial to remain conversant with the latest research and developments. This practice enables me to maintain a robust foundation of knowledge.

Sample 3: Regularly

As the adage goes, “Knowledge is power,” and in my studies, voracious reading is the key to unlocking that power. I dedicate substantial time to perusing diverse sources, which broadens my understanding and equips me with the necessary tools to excel academically.

Sample 4: Regularly

Immersing myself in a plethora of reading materials is an integral aspect of my educational pursuits. By consistently updating my knowledge base, I am better prepared to tackle complex concepts and engage in scholarly discourse with my peers and mentors.

Sample 5: Rarely

Surprisingly, my work necessitates minimal reading, as I predominantly utilize practical skills and hands-on experience to excel in my profession. This practical focus allows me to hone my abilities and perform tasks with efficacy.

Sample 6: Rarely

I engage in a modest amount of reading for my studies, mainly because I rely on alternative learning methods to grasp concepts. This approach enables me to allocate time efficiently and diversify my educational experiences.

Sample 7: Rarely

Although I acknowledge the importance of reading in certain fields, my occupation is more inclined towards verbal communication and interpersonal skills. As a result, I seldom devote extensive periods to reading.

Sample 8: Rarely

Surprisingly, my studies entail a negligible volume of reading. As my coursework emphasizes experiential learning and interactive activities, the need for copious amounts of reading is largely circumvented. This pedagogical approach fosters a more engaging learning environment that places emphasis on real-world applications.

Sample 9: Moderately

I allocate a measured portion of my time to reading for my studies, as I believe that the key to success lies in striking the right balance. Though I do leaf through books and articles, I also partake in group discussions and practical exercises, which, in my opinion, contribute significantly to my overall academic growth.

Sample 10: Moderately

For my studies, I adhere to the adage “quality over quantity” when it comes to reading. By focusing on select, highly relevant materials, I am able to assimilate knowledge effectively without feeling overwhelmed by an excessive volume of information.
